title: Infinitesimal conjugacy of two split-torus homomorphisms
statement: Let $A$ be any commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; its multiplication, inverse and identity satisfy the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] over $S$. For $r\geq0$, put $T=\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ with multiplication of units and $T=S$ if $r=0$. Suppose $f_1,f_2:T\to G$ are $S$-group homomorphisms and $f_1|_{S_0}=f_2|_{S_0}$ as homomorphisms after scalar extension to $A/J$. Then there is $u\in G(A)$ restricting to the identity in $G(A/J)$ such that $\operatorname{Int}(u)\circ f_1=f_2$, where $\operatorname{Int}(u)(g)=ugu^{-1}$ on every test algebra. Neither homomorphism is required to be injective, and no noetherian, field, connectedness or reductivity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf . Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, together with Remark B.2.4, printed p.285: the degree-one Hochschild cohomology of a split torus with quasi-coherent coefficients vanishes. Only conjugacy of two already supplied lifts is asserted here.

proof.text: Put $M=\ker(G(A)\to G(A/J))$, written additively by [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module]. For $d=1,2$ the Laurent algebra $C_d=A[\mathbf Z^{dr}]$ is free over $A$, with basis its Laurent monomials; tensoring any exact sequence with it takes the direct sum of copies of that sequence, so it is flat. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-group-congruence-flat-scalar-extension] to identify $K_{C_d}$ with $M\otimes_A C_d$. Thus its elements are finite Laurent sums with coefficients in $M$, its group law is addition, and scalar extension is substitution in Laurent variables. Conjugation by any $g\in G(C_d)$ becomes a $C_d$-linear automorphism. These assertions use the actual square-zero ideal $JC_d$, not a split extension of $A/J$ by $J$.

source.place: WANTED locally; read online https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/luminysga3smf.pdf . Corollary B.2.6 and proof, printed p.287; Proposition B.2.5, final paragraph, pp.286--287; Remark B.2.4, p.285. The explicit constant-Laurent-coefficient contraction is agent-written.

proof.text:
In $C_1=A[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_r^{\pm1}]$ take the universal torus point $x$ and set $c(x)=f_2(x)f_1(x)^{-1}\in K_{C_1}$; the kernel condition follows from the given equality modulo $J$. Let $\rho_x$ denote conjugation by $f_1(x)$ on this kernel. In $C_2=A[x^{\pm1},y^{\pm1}]$, the homomorphism identities give
$$f_2(xy)f_1(xy)^{-1}=c(x)f_1(x)c(y)f_1(x)^{-1},\qquad c(xy)=c(x)+\rho_x(c(y)).$$
The second identity is the first under the additive kernel identification, using naturality for the substitutions $t\mapsto x,y,xy$. No lifting of a new homomorphism is needed.

proof.text:
Regard $p\in M$ as a point $u\in G(A)$ reducing to the identity. The identity $c(x)=p-\rho_x(p)$ in the additive kernel says multiplicatively
$$f_2(x)f_1(x)^{-1}=u f_1(x)u^{-1}f_1(x)^{-1}.$$
Cancel $f_1(x)^{-1}$ to get $f_2(x)=u f_1(x)u^{-1}$. These are the values of the two morphisms $T\to G$ at the universal point of the affine scheme $T$; affine coordinate maps therefore agree by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Equivalently substitute any units in any test $A$-algebra. This proves the required equality as group-scheme morphisms. For $r=0$ the monomial index set is $\{0\}$ and the same coefficient calculation gives $c=0$; for $J=0$ one has $M=0$ and may take $u=1$.
